description: Preview an assinafy_create_assignment call without sending anything: same arguments, checked against the document and signers. Use it when the user wants to review before sending. Apps-capable hosts render a card whose Send button performs the request; other clients get the summary as text, and the request is sent only after the user confirms.

copy_receivers.description: Signer IDs that only receive a copy.

entries.description: Required for `collect`: field placements per page.

display_settings.description: A field placement rectangle on a document page. Geometry values are pixels in Assinafy's 150-DPI page image, measured from the upper-left corner. Clients must keep the rectangle within the selected page's width and height; the API does not clamp out-of-bounds values.

fontSize.description: Font size in the 150-DPI page-image coordinate system.

height.description: Height of the placement rectangle, in page-image pixels.

left.description: Horizontal distance from the page's left edge, in page-image pixels.

top.description: Vertical distance from the page's top edge, in page-image pixels.

width.description: Width of the placement rectangle, in page-image pixels.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601; default is no expiration. Must be at least one hour in the future.

message.description: Text included in the invitation email.

notification_methods.description: How the signer is told a signature is being requested. **Exactly one method per signer** — the array shape is historical, and sending two returns `400`. The method must also be compatible with `verification_method`: `Email` verification takes `Email`, `Whatsapp` verification takes `Whatsapp`, and `DigitalCertificate` and `IdDocumentFaceMatchBasic` take either. WhatsApp incurs an additional cost and is available only on paid subscriptions. Omit it to have it inferred from `verification_method`, or `{"Email"}` when neither is sent. See **Verification & Notification Methods** for the full pairing table.

verification_method.description: How the signer's identity is verified before signing. `Email` (default) sends a one-time code to the signer's email; `Whatsapp` sends the code over WhatsApp — the verification itself is not billed, but it requires the WhatsApp notification channel, so the signer costs 0.45 credits (available only on paid subscriptions); `DigitalCertificate` has the signer sign with their own ICP-Brasil certificate (A1/A3) — it requires `method: virtual`, the Digital Certificate feature, a CPF or CNPJ in `government_id`, must be alone in its signing step, and is charged 0.5 credits per signer. A CPF requires that person's certificate (an e-CPF, or an e-CNPJ naming them as legal representative); a CNPJ requires an e-CNPJ for that company, from any of its representatives. `IdDocumentFaceMatchBasic` verifies the signer from a photo of their government ID, a photo of them holding it and a liveness check — it requires the ID Document + Face Match feature, the signer must have a valid CPF in `government_id`, and is charged a per-signer fee. Omit to default to `Email`.
